product.name: Automatic diver's watch, 3 hands + date (generic, 21,600 bph)
product.pitch: A self-winding watch that stores the wearer's arm motion in a coiled spring and releases it through a gear train at exactly six beats per second, kept honest by a balance wheel and hairspring, inside a 200 m water-resistant steel case.
evidence: Illustrative design study: an archetypal mass-market automatic movement (Swiss-lever escapement, 21,600 bph, about 41 h reserve, bidirectional pawl-lever winding, quickset date) in a 42 mm steel diver case. The tooth counts are a consistent train checked by calculation; masses and costs are engineering estimates, not measurements of a specific calibre.
Line items group identical or near-identical parts (for example 18 pressed jewels, 16 movement screws); the movement has about 130 physical parts.
DFA handling times use the Boothroyd 'small part' row; real watch assembly under a microscope with tweezers is slower, so the DFA index here is optimistic.
To use this as a template for a real watch: weigh the parts on a 0.001 g balance, count teeth under a loupe, and read the calibre's own parts list.

requirements.metric: Rate -20 / +40 s/day across positions; isochronism within 10 s/day from full wind to 24 h
requirements.how_met: 21,600 bph balance with an index regulator for adjustment; the Fe-Ni self-compensating hairspring keeps the rate stable with temperature

requirements.need: Runs over a weekend off the wrist
requirements.how_met: Barrel turns once per 8 h (80/10 into the centre pinion); 5.1 turns of mainspring give about 41 h

requirements.metric: Full wind after about 8 h of normal wear
requirements.how_met: 3 g off-centre rotor on a ball bearing; pawl lever rectifies both rotation directions into ratchet motion

requirements.metric: 200 m water resistance (ISO 6425 style test); readable in the dark
requirements.how_met: Screw-down crown and caseback with radial gaskets; compressed crystal gasket; lume on hands and indices; unidirectional bezel

requirements.metric: Runs after a 1 m drop onto hardwood (ISO 1413 style)
requirements.how_met: Spring-mounted shock settings on both balance pivots

requirements.need: Survives a phone or bag clasp
requirements.how_met: Fe-Ni hairspring meets the minimum; a silicon hairspring would make this a non-issue (see opportunities)

fmea.mode: Lose compression with age and sunscreen
fmea.effect: Water ingress, rust on the movement
fmea.action: FKM gaskets, pressure test at each service, print 'service every 5 years' in the manual

design_signals.title: A 1:5760 reduction in four meshes
design_signals.evidence: Barrel 80/10, centre 64/8, third 75/10, fourth 84/7. The centre wheel turns once an hour, the fourth once a minute, the escape wheel 12 times a minute, and the barrel once every 8 h.
design_signals.why: Every wheel has a job on the dial (hour, minute, seconds) or in the energy budget (8 h per barrel turn gives the 41 h reserve with about 5 spring turns). Pinions of 7-10 leaves keep the wheels small, at the cost of some engagement friction.

design_signals.title: The pawl lever winds in both directions with two parts
design_signals.evidence: An eccentric on the rotor pinion rocks a lever with two pawls that push the transmission wheel on both strokes.
design_signals.why: Replaces a pair of reverser wheels (each a small clutch of 6-8 parts) and is more efficient at low rotor angles. It is also why this archetype is cheap and robust.

design_signals.title: A slipping bridle instead of a stop
design_signals.evidence: The outer end of the mainspring is a friction bridle against the barrel wall.
design_signals.why: The automatic can never overwind: at full wind the bridle slips. One feature does the job of a separate torque limiter.

design_signals.title: One brass plate locates everything
design_signals.evidence: About 40 bored seats in the main plate hold jewels, pillars and steady pins; the bridges only cap them.
design_signals.why: Holding the critical centre distances in one part is what makes the train mesh without fitting by hand. The plate costs more than any wheel because of it.

design_signals.title: Water resistance lives in four rubber rings
design_signals.evidence: Crystal, caseback and two crown gaskets are the only seals. The steel and the sapphire do no sealing on their own.
design_signals.why: The 200 m rating is a maintenance item, not a property of the case. The rating depends on the cheapest parts in the watch.

opportunities.title: Size the movement to the case
opportunities.change: Bore the case middle to the movement diameter and delete the holder ring
opportunities.impact: One part and one assembly step fewer; the movement seats on metal, not plastic

opportunities.title: Fold the pallet bridge into the train bridge
opportunities.change: One bridge carries the train and the pallet pivots
opportunities.impact: One part and two screws fewer, about 15 s off assembly; the pallet still comes out with the train bridge for service

opportunities.title: Quick-release spring bars
opportunities.change: Spring bars with a lever so the wearer changes straps without a tool
opportunities.impact: The commonest owner repair becomes tool-free; strap sales rise

opportunities.title: Silicon hairspring
opportunities.change: Replace the Fe-Ni hairspring with oxidised silicon
opportunities.impact: Removes the magnetism failure mode and improves temperature stability; needs a new collet and stud

opportunities.title: Date mechanism that cannot jam
opportunities.change: Slip clutch on the date driving wheel
opportunities.impact: Removes the 21:00-03:00 'do not set' warning from the manual

verdict: A textbook mass-market automatic: the gear train, pawl-lever winding and slipping bridle get the most function from the fewest parts, and the brass main plate does the precision work so that the wheels can be cheap. The cost sits in the case, the crystal and the plate rather than in the gears, and assembly is dominated by tiny-part handling, sixteen movement screws, lubrication and regulation. Reliability is set by the four gaskets, the oil and the hairspring's magnetism, not by the steel. A silicon hairspring and a jam-proof date are the upgrades that change the owner experience; the holder ring and the separate pallet bridge are the cost-downs.
